rule: GOAL: Fill the four slots to match the colored frames shown above them. CONTROLS: Click a solid color piece in the bottom tray, then click the corresponding empty slot. RULE: The hollow colored squares at the top indicate exactly which color belongs in each slot. TRAP: Assuming the bottom order matters or that green was correct just because it fit the first slot.

GOAL: Drop the magenta block into the left cup using the blue bar. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the bar in four-cell steps; Space releases the block. RULE: The bar acts as a platform, carrying the block downward until it hits the cup rim. TRAP: Assuming single-cell movement wastes time; remember each key press moves the bar four units.

GOAL: Resize the gray boundary to clear the yellow block by shifting its edges in opposite directions. CONTROLS: Click the top blue handle to widen the top and narrow the bottom; click the bottom handle to reverse. RULE: The boundary acts like a seesaw; one click adjusts both upper and lower widths simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming the gray area is a single sliding panel; it is actually two sections resizing inversely.

GOAL: Navigate the 6x6 room grid to reach the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one logical room per press. RULE: Move only through open gaps; solid walls block passage. TRAP: Thinking the grid is solid; some rooms are missing, forcing longer detours.

GOAL: Reach the blue block to extend the snake. CONTROLS: Left shrinks the tail, Up moves the head, Right grows the head. RULE: Blocks attach when the trail overlaps their cells. TRAP: Moving Up first traps you, as the tail blocks the path.

GOAL: Move the square to the top hole. CONTROLS: Click a spot to drag the square to the ring's center. RULE: The square only moves if the ring covers its edge. TRAP: Aiming for the square's center fails; you must target the boundary.

GOAL: Slide the bottom panel right to align the key with the slot. CONTROLS: One button expands the bottom edge while shrinking the middle. RULE: Each press shifts the bottom edge four units to the right. TRAP: Assuming the middle panel’s shrinking size blocks the bottom expansion.

GOAL: You must grab a specific item and carry it to a marked drop zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step; the space bar picks up or releases the held item. RULE: You must physically walk next to the item, facing it, to grab it, then walk to the target to drop it. TRAP: Do not assume movement commands stack or slide; each arrow press moves only one square, so plan your path step-by-step.

GOAL: Rearrange colored tokens to match a hidden target pattern by swapping pieces between slots. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click another slot to swap their contents. Press Space to submit your arrangement for validation. RULE: The validation system reveals only the first mismatching position, allowing you to correct errors one step at a time. TRAP: Assuming all slots must be filled with unique colors; some slots remain empty or share colors in the final solution.

GOAL: Align three colored keys with their matching gaps in the bar. CONTROLS: Click side buttons to shift panels, moving keys and gaps simultaneously. RULE: All three keys must align with their respective gaps at the same time. TRAP: Assuming keys move independently; they are linked, so moving one affects the others.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored shapes into the correct sequence to clear the board. CONTROLS: Click a shape in the tray, then click a slot to place it; press space to confirm. RULE: Shapes fill slots in reading order, but feeder boxes insert their contents at the port location. TRAP: Assuming all shapes follow the main row order ignores how feeder boxes replace specific ports.

GOAL: Place six colored pieces into two boxes to match a target sequence. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select, click a slot to place, press Space to check. RULE: The port piece's slot index determines the alignment offset for the sequence. TRAP: Assuming the port can go anywhere; its position is fixed by the target's first matching piece.

GOAL: Set all switches to black to guide the plug into the socket. CONTROLS: Click switches to toggle colors; press the ball to execute movement. RULE: Black switches trigger downward motion, filling the gap to nest the plug. TRAP: Thinking only vertical alignment matters; you must activate every switch to ensure full descent.

GOAL: Reach the exit without being caught by the guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in that direction. RULE: The guard lunges instantly if you stand directly to its left or right. TRAP: Thinking you could approach from the side; only vertical entry is safe.

GOAL: Place pieces so two identical triplets appear in the row. CONTROLS: Click tray pieces, then click board slots to place them; press Space to confirm. RULE: The two empty slots must hold identical blue boxes, creating matching three-piece sequences. TRAP: Assuming the boxes could differ or that order didn't matter wasted time finding the unique match.

GOAL: Arrange nested color boxes to match a nine-item target sequence. CONTROLS: Click tray items to place them into specific slots of colored feeder boxes and the main red frame. RULE: Each feeder box starts with a fixed piece; the remaining two slots must be filled to create a valid three-piece group matching the target order. TRAP: Assuming any feeder box could occupy any main slot ignores the fixed starting piece, breaking the sequence alignment.

ESTABLISHED: Slots 0, 1, and 3 accept multiple rotations; slot 4 accepts only one specific rotation. FAILED: Assuming a single canonical rotation for every slot and failing to verify the cursor position before cycling. GOAL IS NOT: Finding a unique orientation for every piece, as multiple orientations satisfy the match condition. CONTROLS: RIGHT moves the cursor to the next slot; UP cycles the current slot's piece through its available rotations.

GOAL: Fit the plug tip into the socket by shrinking it to match the narrow shaft. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug tip horizontally toward the connection point. RULE: The tip must be small enough to pass through the neck before reaching the handle. TRAP: Trying to insert a large tip causes a block; you must resize first.

GOAL: Fill the nested boxes to match the target color sequence. CONTROLS: Click tray pieces, then click slots to place them. RULE: Port frame color indicates its feeder box; ports go in middle slots. TRAP: Thinking ports fill edge slots or link directly to the root box.

GOAL: Rotate five columns to match a hidden pattern, completing the row. CONTROLS: Left and Right move the cursor; Up rotates the selected column upward. RULE: Each column must display a specific shape that pairs with its neighbor, not just any valid domino. TRAP: Assuming a single universal shape for all slots; some columns require unique rotations that break the simple pattern.

GOAL: Shrink the wide plug tip to fit through the narrow neck, then push it up into the handle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicking white pattern cells triggers the shrink evaluation. RULE: The tip must shrink to two units wide before passing the two-unit neck passage. TRAP: Moving the tip up before shrinking jams it against the narrow collar, wasting moves.

GOAL: Navigate a tight corridor to reach the exit while avoiding or capturing guards. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Guards only attacked directly in front of them; approaching from the side or back was safe. TRAP: Assuming guards threatened all adjacent cells caused hesitation and unnecessary detours, wasting valuable moves.

GOAL: Place each cross exactly over matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross three units per press; spacebar switches which cross is active. RULE: The cross’s center must align precisely with the dots’ intersection; arms must not miss any dot. TRAP: Assuming you can fine-tune position one unit at a time; movement is locked to three-unit jumps, so miscounting steps wastes turns.

GOAL: Extend bars to completely cover the plus-shaped sockets. CONTROLS: Clicking lengthens the bar by three pixels. RULE: The bar tip must reach the socket’s far edge to fill it. TRAP: Stopping when the bar merely touches the socket fails; it must overlap the center.

GOAL: Merge two pairs of tiles into larger blocks, then transport them to a final location for a concluding merge. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space moves the nearest block; clicking near two blocks merges them if within range. RULE: Merges require blocks to be close enough, so nudge blocks slightly before combining to ensure success. TRAP: Assuming blocks auto-align perfectly; skipping small nudges causes failed merges and wasted clicks.

GOAL: Cover all target dots with shape outlines. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches to the next piece. RULE: Shapes only move in three-pixel steps, so align centers carefully. TRAP: Assuming any close position works; only exact grid alignment counts as covered.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow block lands inside the yellow dashed frame. CONTROLS: Left arrow rotates the blocks counter-clockwise; right arrow rotates them clockwise. RULE: The yellow block moves one step backward per left click, reaching the target in four moves. TRAP: Assuming the right arrow was faster, as clockwise rotation requires twelve clicks to reach the same spot.

GOAL: Remove all but one piece by jumping over neighbors. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click the landing spot to jump. RULE: Each jump removes the piece jumped over, reducing the total count by one. TRAP: Thinking you must clear the board completely; the goal is actually to leave exactly one piece standing.

GOAL: Match panel D's outer ring colors to its center pattern's gray and white cells. CONTROLS: Click a ring cell to toggle its color between blue and red. RULE: Gray center cells mean blue ring cells; white center cells mean red ring cells. TRAP: Assuming the ring is static or requires complex logic instead of simple color toggling based on the center map.

GOAL: Pass the rope through the ring. CONTROLS: Click a cell to move the head there; the tail follows. RULE: The rope is the straight line between the head and tail. TRAP: Placing the bead in the ring center is wrong; the rope itself must intersect the ring.

GOAL: Match the grid cells to the hidden patterns shown at two centers. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color between blue and orange. RULE: Each pattern dictates the colors of its surrounding eight cells, with overlaps agreeing. TRAP: Assuming the center dot’s color was irrelevant; it signaled the target color for mismatches.

GOAL: Route bars to the target while navigating around fixed obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys extend or retract each colored bar from its anchor point. RULE: Bars cannot overlap obstacles, so you must shorten a bar to slip it through a gap before extending it again. TRAP: Assuming bars must stay fully extended; keeping them short until they clear the obstacle is essential to avoid collision.

GOAL: Slide the bar to cover specific dots, then position the X to clear the rest. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar or X; Space confirms placement. RULE: The bar must fully cover dots to hide them before clearing the board. TRAP: Assuming Space moves the piece; it only locks the current selection, wasting turns if misused.

GOAL: Match each neighbor cell to the center's color rule. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color. RULE: White means match the center; green means differ from the center. TRAP: Assuming green meant match the center, which reversed the logic and wasted clicks.

GOAL: Join the two separate blocks into a single connected shape at the top center. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide blocks until they hit a wall or obstacle. RULE: Blocks merge visually when adjacent, but contact alone does not trigger the level end. TRAP: Assuming the yellow notch is a target. It is a solid wall, not a plug socket.

GOAL: Match target colors by cycling cells through a fixed sequence. CONTROLS: Each click advances a cell one step in the color cycle. RULE: One click equals one state change; calculate steps needed per cell. TRAP: Believing batched clicks continue after completion wastes turns on the next board.

GOAL: Place a yellow token into the frame, triggering absorption, then repeat for the second frame. CONTROLS: Clicking a row rotates all ten cells in that row simultaneously. RULE: Frames vanish once filled, removing the token and reducing the puzzle to a single-object search. TRAP: Believing both tokens must occupy frames simultaneously, which is impossible under the rotation constraints.

ESTABLISHED: Pressing plus flashes both boxes at coverage one; blocked moves flash only the legend box. The yellow bar depletes with actions; red blocks remain unchanged. FAILED: Moving up when blocked did nothing but trigger the legend flash. Repeated attempts to clear the level have exhausted the yellow budget without success. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the icon shape or adjusting the plug's tip height, as these hypotheses proved incorrect during recent reasoning. CONTROLS: The plus button triggers coverage events. Directional inputs move the plug; blocked moves signal status via the legen

GOAL: Guide two blocks to their matching targets without colliding. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Identical blocks merge into one; different blocks slide past each other. TRAP: Assuming blocks stop when hitting each other; they actually pass through or merge, requiring careful positioning to avoid accidental merging.

GOAL: Move the plus shape to cover three orange dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space switches between the X and plus. RULE: Touching a colored square recolors your piece to match it. TRAP: Moving over a square doesn't keep the color unless it is the last one touched.

GOAL: Get the electrified plug into the right-side ring. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active plug; clicks switched which plug was active. RULE: When plugs touched, current teleported the other plug through the wall. TRAP: Believing the dot’s current location was the goal; the target was actually the distant ring.

GOAL: Align the plug with hidden markers to trigger sequence A-B-C. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug one grid step per press. RULE: Markers activate only when the plug fully covers them upon entry, not exit. TRAP: Counting exit steps as triggers wastes moves; only initial entry registers the sequence.

ESTABLISHED: The blue block moves freely on black floor, leaving gray markers upon reversal. The red block is static and blocks the path. FAILED: Moving the blue block toward the red blob causes no reaction; it does not push or interact with the red piece. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the red blob or pushing it out of the way. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue block. Spacebar resets the block to its starting position.

GOAL: Move the yellow token to the yellow frame and the orange token to the orange frame. CONTROLS: Click left or right arrows to rotate tokens clockwise or counter-clockwise within their current cycle. RULE: Shared cells allow tokens to jump between cycles, expanding the reachable area beyond simple loops. TRAP: Assuming tokens stay in separate loops; they actually merge into one large orbit of 870 states.

GOAL: Slide two blocks to touch, then fire the smaller one into the top-left ring, and park the larger one in the bottom-left ring. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block. Clicks activate a block for movement or firing. RULE: A block only fires when its white face touches another block, launching it in that direction. TRAP: Assuming grid steps are one cell; they are three, causing missed alignment and wasted moves.

GOAL: Arrange the scattered tokens into their correct, connected paths. CONTROLS: Click arrows to rotate entire rows or columns, shifting all items within that line. RULE: Rows and columns form single, continuous loops where the end connects directly to the start. TRAP: Assuming edges act as walls rather than portals causes you to miss that items wrap around.

GOAL: Guide the plug to align its tips with the target pads. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug in three-cell steps; collision halts movement. RULE: The plug stops immediately if a tip would overlap a solid pad. TRAP: Assuming you must move down first; moving right early is safe and simpler.

GOAL: Mirror the black shape to cover the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the black shape; its reflection moves in sync. RULE: Horizontal reflection maps columns to 62 minus current column, preserving rows. TRAP: Assuming vertical movement affects only the original, ignoring that the mirror shares the same row coordinates.

GOAL: Paint the top half white to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows orbit the ink container around the block; Space applies the current ink color. RULE: The container must reach the specific side of the block before Space paints that half. TRAP: Assuming arrows move the ink directly; they only rotate the container’s position, requiring precise orbital navigation.

GOAL: Move the player from the start to the green goal tile by jumping over adjacent pieces. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player two spaces in a cardinal direction, requiring both the jumped-over and landing cells to be occupied. RULE: The total number of occupied cells remains constant because the player leaves a tile behind, making the grid layout effectively static for pathfinding. TRAP: Thinking the board changes significantly after each move, when in fact the occupied set is invariant, so you can plan the entire path on the initial grid.

GOAL: Align the gray shape’s edges with the target markers in the black bar. CONTROLS: Click the top blue block to shift the shape’s dividers left; click the bottom blue block to shift them right. RULE: Each blue block click moves the shape one unit in its respective direction. TRAP: Assuming the clicks were cumulative or that other elements like the arrow or bar were interactive.

GOAL: Move the black shape down so its reflection covers the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the currently active object; Spacebar switches which object is active. RULE: The object with white dots is active and moves with arrows; the other object stays fixed. TRAP: Assuming arrows always move the wall. You must press Spacebar first to select the black shape before moving it down.

GOAL: Move the green tip to the target slot by shifting the bottom edge. CONTROLS: Click blue handles to slide adjacent edges in opposite directions. RULE: Top and middle edges trade value; middle and bottom edges trade value. TRAP: Believing the bottom edge cannot rise once the middle edge hits zero.

GOAL: Paint the grid into three distinct colored regions based on row and column sums. CONTROLS: Move the container to an edge, select an ink color, and press space to pour from that direction. RULE: Pours fill contiguous areas from the edge inward until blocked by a different color, overwriting previous layers. TRAP: Believing a single pour creates the final pattern; you must layer colors from different edges to isolate specific zones.

ESTABLISHED: The yellow pin and green knob are fixed in their boxes. The yellow pin never moved, regardless of knob position or switch state. FAILED: Moving the knob to any edge or corner, and toggling blue/red switches to all combinations, produced no changes to the pin or board. GOAL IS NOT: Physically moving the green knob to touch the yellow pin, or closing a visible wire circuit to trigger movement. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green knob within its box; clicking switches toggles blue and red wire orientations.

GOAL: Place three frames so their dots rest on the gray bar. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the assembly; Space detached the current frame. RULE: A frame locks when its dot aligns with a gray section. TRAP: Thinking the whole frame needed to cover the bar; only the dot mattered.

GOAL: Guide the piston through the pipe by setting the correct lever sequence. CONTROLS: Click levers to toggle their up or down state. Click the pump to run the machine. RULE: The machine only completes the cycle if the levers match the required path; otherwise, it reverts. TRAP: Believing the animation showed success when it actually displayed a failed attempt that snapped back to start.

ESTABLISHED: The cross at the top is the goal. The ship fits through the shaft at columns 31-35 if the block at rows 13-17 is removed. FAILED: Moving left to the cross directly is blocked by walls; the ship cannot reach the goal from the side. GOAL IS NOT: A solid barrier to destroy, but a target to touch. CONTROLS: Left/Right moves horizontally. Mouse clicks destroy specific blocks. The ship rises automatically through open vertical paths.

GOAL: Place the L and T shapes so their reflections cover the yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space cycles between pieces. RULE: A piece’s reflection mirrors its position across the center, matching opposite yellow shapes. TRAP: Moving a piece through the central band is safe if it already straddles it, so don’t waste turns rerouting around it.

GOAL: Reach the goal without triggering the charging enemy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one space; special moves jump two spaces. RULE: The enemy charges only when you land two spaces away in its facing row. TRAP: Thinking you can dodge the charge by moving vertically; it kills on contact regardless of distance.

GOAL: Align the ship with the vertical shaft to rise to the top chamber, then navigate to the pink cross. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the ship horizontally in fixed six-column increments. RULE: The ship only fits through gaps matching its exact width; precise alignment is mandatory. TRAP: Assuming the ship is already aligned when it looks close. A six-column offset hid the true gap, wasting time.

GOAL: Align two shapes to mirror a central band and cover hidden targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles to the next piece. RULE: Pieces reflect across the band; matching reflections cover the yellow targets. TRAP: Assuming pieces stay visible; they vanish when perfectly aligned with their reflections.

GOAL: Navigate the player from start to finish while avoiding laser beams emitted by stationary red enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one grid square in the corresponding direction. RULE: Stepping directly onto a red enemy destroys it instantly, clearing its threat zone. TRAP: Assuming walls are solid; some grid cells look empty but are actually occupied, causing moves to fail silently.

GOAL: Rotate five glyphs to match hidden targets. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved cursor; UP rotated glyph; RIGHT advanced slot. RULE: Each slot required a specific dihedral transform applied to its partner. TRAP: Assuming cursor wrapped incorrectly wasted moves before aligning the first slot.

GOAL: Position the bar to catch the falling beam. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar; space drops the beam. RULE: The bar acts as a solid block, stopping the beam where it hits. TRAP: Believing the beam passes through or reflects off the bar wastes moves; it simply stops.

GOAL: Align all piston tips with their target slots. CONTROLS: Click bars to raise or lower adjacent pistons. RULE: A piston cannot rise above the lower of its two neighboring bars. TRAP: Assuming pistons move freely; they are constrained by neighboring bar heights.

GOAL: Move the purple square along the track to reach the ball. CONTROLS: Click a slot on the track to slide the square to that position. RULE: The square travels in a straight line along the track and stops exactly where clicked. TRAP: Believing the white plus is a special target; it is merely a track slot, not a unique goal.

GOAL: Match the target color sequence shown at the top by filling the central slots. CONTROLS: Click a colored block to select it, then click a slot to place it. RULE: Blocks swap positions with the gray placeholders when moved into slots. TRAP: Assuming you could drag blocks directly; you must select first, then place.

GOAL: Extend the yellow bar to reach the target dot. CONTROLS: Click the bottom yellow U-shaped symbol to grow the bar by three units per click. RULE: The symbol opening upward expands the bar; the inverted one shrinks it. TRAP: Assuming the top symbol controls growth wastes moves, as it actually reduces the bar length.

GOAL: Clear all dots by aligning the cross arms with their positions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross; Space switches control between crosses. RULE: Each cross clears only dots matching its color when arms pass over them. TRAP: Believing arms extend infinitely; board edges clamp them, blocking specific alignments.

GOAL: Place the white plus marker inside the dashed target ring. CONTROLS: Click anywhere on the board to instantly move the white plus to that spot. RULE: The square always sits at the midpoint between the white plus and the fixed gray plus. TRAP: Thinking the gray plus was draggable or that the square needed to enter the ring; only the white plus moves.

GOAL: Collect scattered orange dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Space switches between the blue plus and orange X shapes. RULE: The orange X requires a vertical drop followed by a short horizontal shift to align with its target dots. TRAP: Assuming the cursor’s center matches the previous shape’s position; the X’s effective center is offset, causing missed hits.

ESTABLISHED: The tray highlights blocks only when other blocks are connected in a chain to the plug; isolated blocks touching the cord do not light up. FAILED: Extending the cord to touch a single isolated block against the wall did not trigger the highlight. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching the wall with the cord tip or connecting one block at a time. CONTROLS: RIGHT extends the cord; DOWN moves the tip down; LEFT retracts the cord.

GOAL: Guide the L-shaped block to the glowing plus symbol. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the block one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The block wins only when it fully covers the plus marker. TRAP: Assuming the plus was a decorative floor pattern rather than the true objective.

ESTABLISHED: The piston advances one unit per successful match. The trigger requires the green cells to exactly match the diamond shape; an extra green cell prevents activation. FAILED: Clicking the panel center produced no effect. Attempting to match with an extra green cell active did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the left edge of the shaft. CONTROLS: Clicking matches colors to move the piston. Clicking panel dots may toggle target patterns.

GOAL: Position three shapes to cover all scattered dots simultaneously. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; SPACE cycles to the next shape. RULE: Each shape covers dots within its specific geometric range, like a diamond’s radius or an X’s arms. TRAP: Assuming shapes work independently; they must overlap their coverage zones to clear every dot at once.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align the yellow tile with the yellow bracket. CONTROLS: Red button rotates the ring counterclockwise; green rotates clockwise. RULE: Each click moves tiles one slot; match color to bracket to win. TRAP: Assuming clockwise rotation wastes clicks; red actually moves tiles counterclockwise.

GOAL: Guide two spiraling tokens to meet at the top center. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both tokens simultaneously; space resets the level. RULE: Tokens follow mirrored spiral paths inward, requiring synchronized movement to align at the summit. TRAP: Assuming independent control; moving one token without considering the other’s mirrored path leads to dead ends.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens in the correct sequence to pass the reveal scan. CONTROLS: Click a token to select it, click another to swap them, and press Space to test the arrangement. RULE: The scan reveals tokens in a specific order, stopping at the first mismatch to show the correct position. TRAP: Assuming the scan follows a simple left-to-right row order; the red row's final token is actually read last.

GOAL: Move two tokens to meet at a single safe tile without touching spikes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both tokens simultaneously in the same direction. RULE: Walls block movement safely, but spikes instantly kill if stepped on. TRAP: Assuming blocked moves prevent death; if one token hits a spike, you die even if the other is blocked.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over adjacent neighbors into empty spaces. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a valid landing spot to jump and capture the passed peg. RULE: Jumps must be horizontal or vertical, landing exactly two spaces away over a single opposing peg. TRAP: Clicking an invalid landing spot deselects your piece instead of moving it, wasting your turn.

GOAL: Move plus shapes to form target shapes. CONTROLS: Click a plus to activate it, then click a destination to move it. RULE: The center of the final shape must align with the target ring. TRAP: Assuming you must move every plus once; only the active one moves per turn.

GOAL: Place two yellow tiles into fixed bracket slots on the right. CONTROLS: Red buttons shift rows left or rotate the ring counter-clockwise; green buttons shift rows right or rotate the ring clockwise. RULE: Row shifts affect only horizontal lines, while ring rotations move tiles along the perimeter path, allowing precise positioning. TRAP: Assuming green always moves tiles forward caused errors, as green actually shifts rows right and rotates the ring clockwise, opposite to the red button's direction.

GOAL: Guide the yellow tile to the yellow bracket and the orange tile to the orange bracket. CONTROLS: Left and right buttons rotate the corresponding ring clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Tiles can only switch rings at the shared cells where the two circles intersect. TRAP: Assuming tiles stay in their starting ring prevents crossing; you must move them through the overlap.

GOAL: Slide the red plug left to touch the green pins. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug one grid step. RULE: Align the plug tips with the pin gaps to avoid collision. TRAP: Moving too far right causes the plug to overlap the socket.

GOAL: Align the two side pieces against the central divider to complete the shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move both side pieces simultaneously; Left and Right shift them horizontally. RULE: The pieces move toward each other on Right and away on Left, stopping at the center wall. TRAP: Believing the pieces move independently or that vertical movement was required, which wasted actions.

GOAL: Move token to yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move token; click colors rotate bars. RULE: Token passes only through open paths; rotated bars create new routes. TRAP: Assuming checker blocks path; it only blocks when token must traverse it, not when already past.

ESTABLISHED: The white plug is seated in the left ring. The black plug is stranded on the right panel. FAILED: Seating only one plug. Pushing the black plug right from its stranded position. GOAL IS NOT: Seating the white plug alone. CONTROLS: Pressing a direction moves the active plug until it hits a wall or another object.

ESTABLISHED: The snake's head vanished, shifting the entire body six cells forward along its path while preserving total length. The box now occupies the head's former position. The tail retreated, freeing the entrance cell. The maze path to the goal is now open and clear of the snake's body. FAILED: Moving the box down into the remaining vertical red line. This direction is blocked because the target cell contains red pixels from the snake's shifted body. GOAL IS NOT: Eating the snake's head again. The head is already gone. Repeated consumption is unnecessary because the body shift has alread

GOAL: Move the active plug into the matching hole. CONTROLS: Click a plug to make it active; use arrows to move the active plug. RULE: Only the plug with the white dot responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Assuming arrows always move the same plug regardless of which one you clicked last.

GOAL: Match the monitor's red tile pattern by toggling the screen panel. CONTROLS: Click red or blue tiles to flip their color; click the center to submit. RULE: The small thumbnail in the monitor panel shows the exact target configuration you must replicate. TRAP: Assuming clicking the monitor or side panels changes the goal; only the central grid is interactive for matching.

GOAL: Make the large grid match the small thumbnail exactly by turning specific tiles red. CONTROLS: Click a tile to toggle its color between blue and red. RULE: The thumbnail is the target; every white cell there must be red, and every grey cell must be blue. TRAP: Assuming only the center tile needed matching; the off-center tile in the right column also required toggling to red.

GOAL: Align matching letters across two horizontal rows by shifting them in opposite directions. CONTROLS: Red left arrows shift both rows left; green right arrows shift both rows right. RULE: The grid wraps horizontally between rows, so a tile exiting one row's edge enters the other row's opposite edge. TRAP: Assuming rows wrap internally to themselves wastes time; they actually exchange tiles across the two rows.

GOAL: Guide the falling block to the target by reflecting its path through a mirror. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space switches control between the block and the mirror. RULE: The mirror flips the block’s position horizontally, so align the mirror first, then drop the block. TRAP: Believing you must move the block directly to the target, ignoring the mirror’s required pre-alignment.

GOAL: Light up the entire grid by clicking specific red tiles to turn them orange. CONTROLS: Click any red tile to toggle its state to orange. RULE: Each click illuminates the tile and its immediate neighbors in a cross shape. TRAP: Assuming all red tiles need clicking; strategic placement covers multiple tiles at once, solving the puzzle in far fewer moves.

GOAL: Paint specific target cells orange while leaving others blue. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color from blue to red to orange and back to blue. RULE: Only the designated target cells need to be orange; all other cells must remain blue. TRAP: Assuming non-target cells must be red to satisfy the puzzle, which wastes clicks and requires extra steps to revert them to blue.

GOAL: Align the slider's yellow tip with the yellow marker on the bar. CONTROLS: Click the top blue block to move right; click the bottom blue block to move left. RULE: Matching colors indicates the target position for the slider. TRAP: Clicking the black bar or the slider itself does nothing; only the blue side blocks work.

GOAL: Rotate the red cross to open a vertical path, then guide the token to the yellow square. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicking the red plug rotates the cross 90 degrees. RULE: The token fits only in gaps matching its 2x2 size; rotation aligns arms to create these gaps. TRAP: Assuming the cross stays horizontal; failing to rotate it blocks the upward route, forcing wasted moves.

GOAL: Place two mirrored blocks onto their matching yellow target shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; Space switches which block is active. RULE: A block is solved only when it and its mirror image both cover their respective targets. TRAP: Focusing only on the bottom block’s position; neglecting the mirror’s alignment wastes moves since both must match simultaneously.

GOAL: Guide the box to the exit while navigating a moving snake. CONTROLS: Arrows move the box; Space toggles a recording ghost that repeats your path. RULE: The snake only retracts when the box occupies its head cell, requiring precise timing. TRAP: Believing the ghost clears automatically; you must move the box to make the recording non-empty before toggling Space again to remove it.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking green blocks destroys them. Clicking water or open space does nothing. The bubble floats upward to the highest reachable ceiling. FAILED: Clicking water, empty air, or the bubble itself had no effect. Destroying blocks below the bubble did not cause it to rise further. GOAL IS NOT: Simply destroying all green blocks, as the level did not clear when the path was blocked by solid walls. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks target specific grid cells to destroy breakable blocks. Arrow keys adjust horizontal position.

GOAL: Align reflections of two combs and a stem by moving a mirror and shifting pieces horizontally. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles selection between the mirror and the two pieces. RULE: Reflections form a mirror image across the mirror's center line, requiring precise vertical positioning and horizontal alignment. TRAP: Believing objects block each other during movement; the mirror passes through pieces freely, allowing vertical placement before horizontal adjustments.

ESTABLISHED: The panel is not the target. Painting the block's top half purple did not clear the level. The roller's reach is limited, leaving the block's bottom center unpaintable. FAILED: Assuming the panel shows the goal. Trying to paint the bottom half. Matching the block's top half exactly to the assumed target without other conditions. GOAL IS NOT: Simply replicating the panel's pattern on the block. Painting only the top half purple is insufficient for completion. CONTROLS: SPACE rotates the roller, changing the paint band's angle and coverage area on the block.

GOAL: Use four clicks to align moving bars and clear the middle white region. CONTROLS: Click top buttons to shift the upper gray bar; click the bottom handle to slide the lower white block. RULE: The handle pushes the white block left, while top buttons move the gray bar to reveal or cover space. TRAP: Assuming top buttons always work; they become blocked if the white block is already pushed fully to the edge.

GOAL: Place the block into the right tray slot. CONTROLS: Arrows move the core; Space attaches or detaches the block. RULE: The block stays attached while you move, pushing or pulling it along. TRAP: Assuming you can drop the block from any angle; you must face it directly to release.

GOAL: Guide the blue token from the upper-left to the green target in the lower-right corner. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token one square per press. RULE: Movement is strictly single-step; you cannot leap over obstacles or empty gaps. TRAP: Assuming jumps are allowed wastes actions testing invalid moves; stick to simple step-by-step navigation.

GOAL: Set each of five columns to its target glyph within the action limit. CONTROLS: Left and right move the cursor; up and down cycle the current column’s glyph. RULE: Each column follows a fixed cyclic order, so moving toward the nearest direction minimizes steps. TRAP: Assuming all columns cycle identically wastes actions; verify each column’s unique sequence before committing to a direction.

GOAL: Guide the bubble to touch the pink star to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click blocks to destroy obstacles; use arrow keys to move the bubble. RULE: The bubble pops the star only when its blue center directly touches the star's center. TRAP: Do not assume the black outline counts as a collision; only the blue pixels interact with the target.

GOAL: Rotate the roller to vertical, then press space to print. CONTROLS: Mouse selects the tool; arrow keys rotate the roller; space applies ink. RULE: The roller only rotates between 45° clockwise and 135° clockwise using up and down keys. TRAP: Assuming up rotates past 45° clockwise to vertical; use the left key to reach 0° instead.

GOAL: Guide the purple square to the blue core center. CONTROLS: Click a spot to jump the square to that location. RULE: The jump distance is limited; longer hops fail silently and waste moves. TRAP: Assuming you can jump directly to the target; you must chain smaller, successful hops.

GOAL: Align the arch with the cup to complete the structure. CONTROLS: Top toggles steer left or right; vertical toggles steer up or down; both together force a downward move. RULE: Each keyframe applies one movement based on its specific toggle combination. TRAP: Assuming moves were permanent during the preview animation; they reset until the final click commits the correct path.

GOAL: Fill the four empty slots in the exact color order shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a colored tile at the bottom to select it, then click an empty slot to place that color. RULE: You must match the sequence displayed above; each placement consumes one tile from the bottom tray. TRAP: Assuming tiles swap or move automatically. They do not; you must manually select each specific color before placing it.

GOAL: Position the bar and pour liquid to fill the cup notch without wasting any drops. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar horizontally; Space drops the liquid. RULE: Liquid spreads across the bar and pours off both ends, so the bar must catch it all. TRAP: Assuming liquid stays put; it flows off the edges, so misaligned bars cause spills and failure.

GOAL: Move the token to the green target without being caught by the red block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token one step in that direction. RULE: The red block moves two spaces toward the token if they share a row or column. TRAP: Assuming walls block attacks; they do not, so direct line-of-sight proximity is deadly.

GOAL: Reach the exit by navigating around hazards and using walls to stop movement. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the token in that direction until it hits a wall or obstacle. RULE: The token moves in one continuous straight line per input, stopping only at boundaries. TRAP: Assuming single-step movement leads to overshooting targets or hitting deadly enemies unexpectedly.

GOAL: Merge blocks into a yellow square centered in the ring. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the nearest block toward that spot. RULE: The block closest to your click moves, then merges if within range. TRAP: Thinking the circle itself was the target; it is only a placement zone.

GOAL: Balance three liquid bars by moving units between them until they reach specific target heights. CONTROLS: Click buttons between bars to transfer two units from the left bar to the right bar. RULE: Each transfer requires the source bar to stay above a minimum level and the destination below a maximum level. TRAP: Assuming you could freely shrink the middle bar to allow more inflow, when its own capacity limits blocked the path.

GOAL: Connect the glowing tip to the head to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the tip; clicking the card sets the pattern; clicking grid cells activates lights. RULE: The pattern must physically touch the head to transfer energy and win. TRAP: Thinking alignment mattered more than proximity; retracting the tip fully left was the key, not matching shapes.

GOAL: Shrink the large tip to a small square, then move it through the narrow channel to the head. CONTROLS: Click card cells to transfer the pattern and shrink the tip; use arrow keys to move the tip. RULE: The tip must be small enough to fit through the gap, requiring a transfer before moving up. TRAP: Assuming the shrunk tip aligns perfectly with the channel; it often shifts left, requiring horizontal adjustment before moving up.

ESTABLISHED: The cord pushes all blocks in swept rows when extended. Retracting the cord avoids pushing distant blocks. FAILED: Moving the plug with an extended cord causes unwanted cascades among parked blocks. GOAL IS NOT: A single sweep that moves all target blocks to their slots simultaneously without side effects. CONTROLS: Extending or retracting the cord moves the plug and pushes blocks in the affected rows.

GOAL: Place two distinct shapes precisely onto two separate target circles to clear the board. CONTROLS: Click coordinates to move the active piece toward the selected target location. RULE: A piece counts as placed only if its center lands exactly on or covers the circle's core. TRAP: Assuming the grid allows perfect geometric centering; parity issues often force slight offset placements to succeed.

GOAL: Cover all colored dots using two cross-shaped cursors. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross three spaces per press; Spacebar switches control between cursors. RULE: A dot disappears only when a matching-colored cross arm passes directly over it. TRAP: Assuming one cursor solves the puzzle; you must switch control to cover dots of both colors.

GOAL: Move the red knob to align with the cross center. CONTROLS: Click buttons to shift the knob or resize the bar. RULE: The knob must sit exactly on the cross's center point. TRAP: Assuming the knob simply rests at the bar's bottom; it actually sits one unit above the bottom edge.

GOAL: Merge two pieces into a Y and place it on the target circle. CONTROLS: Click a piece to move it a fixed distance toward your cursor. RULE: Pieces merge automatically when they touch, forming the required shape. TRAP: Assuming the moving ring was a target; it was a hazard to avoid.

GOAL: Guide the glowing tip down the side stub to connect with the head. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the tip along the path. RULE: Proximity counts as connection; you do not need to merge inside the frame. TRAP: Believing the tip must move left into the center blocked progress, when simply reaching the bottom of the side stub completed the level.

GOAL: Move the X to the target using the fewest moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the X one space; Space confirms placement. RULE: The bar decrements every three moves, so the budget is generous, not strict. TRAP: Assuming the bar meant a hard limit of 64 moves, causing unnecessary panic and rushed, suboptimal paths.

GOAL: Swap the white diamond onto the ring center using the gray diamond as a pivot. CONTROLS: Click the gray diamond to swap its position with the white diamond. RULE: The white diamond instantly teleports to the gray diamond's location, displacing the gray to the white's previous spot. TRAP: Believing you must drag the white diamond directly; it only moves when swapping with the gray click target.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align matching colors with the side arrows. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to spin the ring clockwise; click the green arrow for counter-clockwise. RULE: Each arrow only moves the ring when its target slot holds the color the arrow points to. TRAP: I thought clicking the ring blocks rotated them individually, but only the side arrows move the whole loop.

GOAL: Rotate the block to match the target shape using collected plus signs. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; collecting pluses rotated the block 90 degrees. RULE: The level completed only when the block's orientation matched the target exactly. TRAP: Assuming the block could enter the box before the shape aligned wasted moves.

GOAL: Move the diamond shape to its target position. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; Space selects the next shape. RULE: Select the diamond first, then move it directly to the marked spot. TRAP: Relying on visual markers can mislead you if overlaps obscure the true center; trust the selection logic instead.

GOAL: Extend the orange shape to size 26 and the sky to size 26 while shrinking yellow to 2. CONTROLS: Click orange or sky to grow by 3; click yellow or green to shrink by 3. RULE: Shapes cannot overlap; the sky can only grow into space vacated by yellow. TRAP: Attempting to grow the sky before yellow fully retracts causes a collision and wastes moves.

GOAL: Match the highlighted panel to a hidden target pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a block in the active panel toggles its color between blue and red. RULE: Only the panel with the bright frame accepts input; others are static references. TRAP: Believing clicks affect neighboring blocks or other panels, causing wasted moves on inactive areas.

GOAL: Paint specific grid cells orange to match the target pattern defined by the two icons. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color between blue and orange. RULE: Each icon dictates the required color for the eight cells surrounding it; overlapping zones must agree. TRAP: Assuming all visible white cells needed clicking, or ignoring that the icons themselves are fixed and unchangeable.

GOAL: Seat two sliding blocks into matching rings to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click a block to select it, then use arrows to shift it three spaces. RULE: Blocks slide three spaces per press, stopping only at walls or other blocks. TRAP: Assuming rings block movement causes errors; they are targets, not obstacles.

GOAL: Turn all target cells orange to match the hidden pattern. CONTROLS: Click any grid cell to toggle its color between red and orange. RULE: Icons act as clues; a white marker means the neighbor is orange, while a green marker means it is red. TRAP: Assuming clicks only work on red cells; remember that clicking an orange cell incorrectly turns it back to red.

GOAL: Reduce the number of pegs to exactly one. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click an empty spot to jump over an adjacent peg into that empty spot. RULE: A jump is only legal if you leap directly over a neighboring peg into an immediately vacant hole. TRAP: Clicking an empty hole first does nothing; you must always select the jumping peg before choosing the destination.

ESTABLISHED: The arch shape is fixed. Two blue pieces exist. The black area is currently one connected region. FAILED: Moving pieces to top corners, creating symmetry, or splitting the black area into unequal halves did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply separating the black shape into two parts or achieving rotational symmetry. CONTROLS: Directional keys move the blue pieces one step at a time within the black area.

GOAL: Move two pieces along tracks to form the letter "B". CONTROLS: Click buttons labeled "BIG" or "R26" with "+1" or "-1" to shift pieces along their respective paths. RULE: The number at the end of the button name determines direction: "+1" moves forward, "-1" moves backward. TRAP: Assuming the last character determines direction fails; use the explicit sign symbol before the number to avoid moving the wrong way.

GOAL: Match the hidden color pattern exactly. CONTROLS: Clicking cycles cell colors between blue, red, and orange. RULE: Icons mark cells that must match the icon’s color; others must not. TRAP: Assuming ambiguous cells stay blue; they must be changed to a non-icon color.

GOAL: Place the two pieces symmetrically across the arch's central axis. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selected piece one step in that direction. RULE: The level cleared only when the pieces formed a perfect mirror image around the center line. TRAP: Trying to make the black background symmetric failed; only the piece positions mattered for the win.

GOAL: Move the diamond to the ring by sliding it over the black floor. CONTROLS: Click a direction to slide the selected piece until it hits a wall or object. RULE: Pieces only slide on black tiles; water and green patches block movement. TRAP: Believing you can stop mid-slide or jump over water, which wastes moves.

GOAL: Guide the plug to mate with the socket by aligning its prongs with the contact pins. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug three units per press in the chosen direction. RULE: The plug locks into place when its red tips touch the stationary pins without overlapping them. TRAP: Assuming the plug can pass through the pins to reach the socket wall wastes moves; it stops upon contact.

GOAL: Guide two colored markers to their matching brackets by rotating two interlocking rings. CONTROLS: Left and right arrow pairs rotate each ring independently in opposite directions. RULE: The rings share two intersection cells, allowing markers to cross from one track to the other. TRAP: Assuming the visible ellipses are the tracks; the actual paths are diagonal loops crossing through the center.

GOAL: Guide both pieces into the central divider cell simultaneously to merge them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both characters at once; if a wall blocks one, that character stays put while the other moves. RULE: Only a synchronized arrival at the exact center triggers victory; independent movement is insufficient. TRAP: Assuming hazards are passable wastes moves; they block movement just like walls, requiring careful routing to avoid dead ends.

ESTABLISHED: The token starts at the origin. A red trail connects a 3x3 head to a solid square. Movement is grid-based. FAILED: Moving down from the trail's end did not push the solid square. Navigating to the head did not trigger an immediate win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the red trail's head or the solid square's current position. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token one step. The spacebar resets the token to the start.

GOAL: Move yellow to the center and orange to the bottom by shifting two intersecting tracks. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the entire vertical or horizontal track one step in that direction. RULE: Tokens only move if they sit on the track being shifted; intersections allow transfers. TRAP: Thinking arrows move individual tokens; they actually shift the whole track, carrying all tokens on it.

GOAL: Seat four blocks into matching rings by sliding them into place. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block; clicks select a different block. RULE: Blocks slide until hitting a wall or another block, never stopping mid-path. TRAP: Assuming a block stops when aligned with a ring; it actually slides through to the far edge.

GOAL: Reach target colors by pressing three special tiles and clicking others. CONTROLS: Click tiles to toggle color. Press special tiles to toggle themselves and four neighbors. RULE: Special tiles must be pressed once because their icons dictate the opposite color. TRAP: Assuming neighbor toggles block independent fixes; they don’t, as you can compensate with individual clicks.

GOAL: Move the shape to perfectly cover the matching yellow zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the piece one step at a time. RULE: The piece must align exactly with the target shape and position. TRAP: Thinking you need to avoid the target; overlapping it is the only way to win.

GOAL: Guide the token into the yellow core to win. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token; clicking the red node rotates the arm. RULE: The arm must be vertical to allow upward travel through the blue body. TRAP: Believing the arm could rotate while blocking the path, or that the core was accessible from the start.

GOAL: Align the yellow knob with the black bar's notch by shifting the vertical walls. CONTROLS: Clicking blue buttons moves the walls; the knob moves with the wall it attaches to. RULE: The top button shifts the upper wall left and lower wall right; the bottom button reverses this. TRAP: Assuming the knob is a separate piece to drag; it is fixed to the wall and only moves when the wall shifts.

GOAL: Move the bottom wall to align the knob with the notch without letting the middle wall vanish. CONTROLS: Top buttons shift upper walls; bottom buttons shift lower walls, affecting the middle wall's width. RULE: The knob must precisely overlap the notch, and every wall must retain at least one pixel of width. TRAP: Assuming walls can shrink to zero; a vanished wall blocks movement, so interleave clicks to maintain buffer space.

GOAL: Move the charcoal block down to cover the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move both blocks simultaneously; SPACE toggles movement modes. RULE: SPACE unlocks vertical movement but inverts the horizontal direction mapping. TRAP: Assuming vertical controls work immediately wastes time; you must press SPACE first to enable them.

GOAL: Reach the designated goal tile by navigating the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character. RULE: Moves are exactly two tiles; the intermediate tile is skipped, and the landing tile must be empty or the goal. TRAP: Assuming the character slides until hitting a wall; it actually stops after exactly two steps.

ESTABLISHED: The board is 64x64. Water flows downward and settles. Crates float on water surfaces. An air pocket exists at the bottom right. FAILED: Right movement caused a sudden, unexplained redistribution of water and crates, resembling a viewport scroll or glitch. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the player right to exit. CONTROLS: Right arrow moves the player. Click creates water. Undo reverses actions.

GOAL: Guide the falling block into the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows steer the piece; Space locks it in place. RULE: Pieces rotate and shift instantly upon landing. TRAP: Assuming the piece stops exactly where it started; friction shifts it right.

GOAL: Paint the top five rows of the purple block white. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the piston around its anchor. Space fires the piston's block to paint cells. Clicks set the block's color. RULE: Only firing paints cells; rotation moves the piston without marking the grid. TRAP: Believing rotating the piston from the side paints the path it sweeps, wasting time checking for accidental marks.

GOAL: Align five water columns to specific target heights to unlock the exit. CONTROLS: Clicking a column shifts water levels in adjacent neighbors, altering overall balance. RULE: Total water volume is conserved; adjust individual columns only by redistributing from others. TRAP: Assuming clicks only affect the clicked column; ignoring neighbor effects leads to chaotic, unsolvable states.

GOAL: Move the piece to the distant target core. CONTROLS: Clicking near the piece moves it; clicking far away teleports it. RULE: Teleport works only if the click is within eight steps of the piece center. TRAP: Believing any far click teleports wastes time; distant clicks fail silently.

ESTABLISHED: The dial holds six R-glyphs and one distractor, matching the six L-glyph pairs in the top key. FAILED: Assuming the check is rotation-sensitive; dial rotations do not consistently match blue row rotations, making strict rotation matching impossible for all slots. GOAL IS NOT: A solution requiring identical shape and rotation between blue and pink rows, as the dial’s fixed rotations prevent this for every slot. CONTROLS: Pressing UP cycles through the dial entries, changing the slot’s glyph class while rotation remains fixed per entry.

GOAL: Reach the exit at the far end of the top row. CONTROLS: Arrows move two spaces in the chosen direction. RULE: Landing on a monster forces it to jump away, clearing the path. TRAP: Avoiding the monster blocks your route; you must land directly on it to proceed.

GOAL: Match five bracket glyphs to specific classes using a shared rotating dial. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor and rotated the dial; UP/DOWN changed the glyph class. RULE: Each class appeared exactly once in the cycle, so the current glyph revealed the dial's hidden position. TRAP: Assuming the starting glyph's index was zero; it was random, requiring calculation from the class rather than the visual order.

GOAL: Route the plug to the cup by setting switch directions. CONTROLS: Click bars to toggle their color; click stems to toggle theirs. RULE: The bar-stem color pair dictates movement: specific combinations trigger Down, Left, or Right moves. TRAP: Assuming switches were static; you must actively flip bars and stems to align the path downward.

GOAL: Fill four empty slots with colored blocks to match a specific pattern. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click an empty slot to place it. RULE: The order of colors in the top bar dictates which color goes into which slot, left to right. TRAP: Believing you could place colors in any order or that selecting a color counted as a step, causing wasted actions.

GOAL: Eliminate three monsters while avoiding their deadly front-facing rays. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one square; landing on a monster eats it. RULE: Monsters attack only the two squares directly in front of them, not behind or sideways. TRAP: Eating a monster requires approaching from its blind spot; entering its front ray kills you instantly.

GOAL: Rotate each yellow slot to match the target glyph sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP rotates the current slot’s dial forward. RULE: The dial cycles through seven glyphs in a fixed order; counting steps reveals the shortest rotation. TRAP: Assuming the dial resets per slot wastes time; the rotation order is consistent across all positions.

GOAL: Sort scattered colors into nested boxes by filling every slot correctly. CONTROLS: Click swatches to select, click slots to place, and press space to confirm. RULE: Green frames define the third slot, forcing a specific flattened reading order. TRAP: Assuming simple top-to-bottom sorting ignores visual nesting, causing immediate placement errors.

GOAL: Guide the falling block to land precisely within the castle notch. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar horizontally; Space drops the block. RULE: The block falls straight down, so the bar must be positioned to catch it exactly over the target gap. TRAP: Believing the block could be steered mid-air or that the bar could move after the drop began.

GOAL: Map seven palette colors to specific slots, accounting for two expanded zones that shift subsequent positions. CONTROLS: Click a bottom swatch to select it, click a target slot to place it, and press Space to submit. RULE: Expanding boxes displace later single slots, so count positions carefully rather than assuming fixed spacing. TRAP: Assuming all slots are single-width leads to misplaced colors; the expanded zones consume two slots each.

GOAL: Move the distant piece to merge with the stationary one. CONTROLS: Click a grid spot to move the active piece toward that point. RULE: Pieces merge when their centers are within four squares of each other. TRAP: Believing you must click directly on the target piece; aiming too close causes an overlap error instead of a merge.

GOAL: Align the sliding bars to the center crosshair. CONTROLS: Click arrows to extend bars toward the target. RULE: Bars stop growing exactly when their ends touch the crosshair center. TRAP: Assuming you must push past the center; overshooting is impossible, so stop clicking once contact is made.

GOAL: Align nested colors with the legend order by placing a frame. CONTROLS: Click palette colors to fill slots; click the frame to nest boxes. RULE: The nested box’s position in the parent dictates where its colors appear in the final sequence. TRAP: Assuming nested colors stay grouped at the end; they actually interleave based on the parent slot index.

GOAL: Map the bottom yellow row to the top blue row using the key cards. CONTROLS: Arrows shifted the active slot’s color class through a fixed cycle. RULE: Each yellow card mapped to a specific blue card, dictating the target class for each slot. TRAP: Pressing blindly without verifying the cycle length led to misaligned slots and wasted moves.

GOAL: Arrange solids and frames to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click items to select, click slots to place, press space to confirm. RULE: The pattern requires a specific sequence of items to align correctly. TRAP: Assuming frames could be placed anywhere without checking the resulting sequence match.

GOAL: Guide the hero to the exit while dodging a patrolling orange enemy and a stationary red threat. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to jump exactly two cells in any direction. RULE: Enemies move once for every jump you make; the red lunges only if you land in its line of sight. TRAP: Assuming the red moves like the orange; it stays put until you trigger its attack, so stay out of its front ray.

GOAL: Arrange nested boxes so their flattened color sequence matches the target legend. CONTROLS: Drag frames and solids into empty slots; press space to verify the solution. RULE: Each parent slot expands to a child box, preserving left-to-right order in the final list. TRAP: Assuming solid colors determine box placement; only the frame type dictates which box fills the slot.

GOAL: Transform the bottom blue row into yellow using two chained color mappings. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the cursor; Up cycled the current tile’s color. RULE: Blue tiles map to pink, then pink to yellow; apply both steps to get the target. TRAP: Assuming direct blue-to-yellow mapping wastes moves; you must route through pink to find the correct yellow glyph.

GOAL: Move two colored crosses so their arms cover all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift a cross’s position; Space swaps which cross is active. RULE: Arms must align precisely with dot centers; overlapping other shapes is allowed and harmless. TRAP: Assuming one cross covering its dots wins; both crosses must simultaneously satisfy their conditions to clear the level.

GOAL: Match the target color sequence by arranging blocks and frames. CONTROLS: Click palette items to fill slots, click placed items to remove them, and press space to submit the answer. RULE: Hollow frames nest their internal slots at that position, expanding the sequence to match the legend exactly. TRAP: Assuming frames are just colors; they actually contain hidden slots that must be filled to complete the pattern.

GOAL: Place the white and gray markers so their midpoint lands exactly on the target ring. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the white marker to that spot, swapping places with the gray marker. RULE: The puzzle solves when the invisible center point between the two markers aligns with the goal. TRAP: Avoiding the gray border area is critical; landing on gray edges breaks the puzzle's logic.

GOAL: Center three colored markers on their matching dot targets to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected marker; the space bar cycles to the next marker. RULE: You must select the correct marker before moving it, as controls affect only the active piece. TRAP: Believing every move consumes a step limit; the timer is generous, so prioritize correct selection over speed.

ESTABLISHED: The wire tip stays adjacent to the blue socket, never passing through it. Blue moves only when pushed right, not pulled left. FAILED: Pressing LEFT did not drag the blue socket back toward the plug. GOAL IS NOT: Threading the wire through the socket to drag it along. CONTROLS: RIGHT extends the wire, pushing adjacent sockets one cell right. LEFT retracts the wire without moving sockets.

GOAL: Guide the cursor from the arm tip into the handle’s blue core. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor two cells per press. RULE: The cursor can only travel through gray regions, stopping at black barriers. TRAP: Believing the cursor could paint the reference pattern instead of navigating to the handle.

GOAL: Guide both squares to the top row. CONTROLS: Arrows move the left square normally, but mirror the right square horizontally. RULE: Horizontal inputs push the squares apart or together; vertical inputs move them both the same way. TRAP: Assuming both squares move identically when pressing Left or Right wastes time.

GOAL: Clear the level by shrinking the large shape down to a two-by-two block that fits the target neck. CONTROLS: Click white cells to trigger the shrink; use arrow keys to move the resulting block. RULE: Shrinking compresses the shape’s color pattern, preserving the relative arrangement of halves in the new smaller cursor. TRAP: Assuming the block keeps its original position; it shifts, so check alignment before moving to avoid getting stuck on walls.

GOAL: Rotate the dial to match the target symbol, then enter the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; stepping on plus signs rotates the dial. RULE: The dial only changes when you step on a plus marker, not automatically. TRAP: Do not assume matching the symbol ends the level; you must physically walk into the exit box.

GOAL: Place the yellow tile into the yellow bracketed corner slot. CONTROLS: The red arrow rotates tiles counterclockwise; the green arrow rotates them clockwise. RULE: The bracket color matches the required tile color, identifying the specific target slot. TRAP: Assuming the goal was to exit through the green arrow wasted actions on the wrong direction.

GOAL: Move the cross, diamond, and bar to cover all target dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space cycles selection. RULE: Only the currently selected piece responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Assuming all pieces move simultaneously wastes turns; switch focus explicitly.

GOAL: Guide two blue squares from the top corners down to the bottom center, ensuring they merge at the designated finish point. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both squares simultaneously in the chosen direction; they stop if blocked by walls or each other. RULE: Movement is simultaneous and rigid; you cannot move one square independently, forcing synchronized navigation around obstacles. TRAP: Assuming you can start from the inner edge; the squares actually begin at the outermost available positions, changing the initial path.

GOAL: Move yellow tiles to specific spots on the perimeter ring. CONTROLS: Click side arrows to rotate the outer loop or slide inner rows left or right. RULE: Tiles shift only when pushed into an empty space; rotation direction depends on arrow color. TRAP: Assuming rows shift independently of the loop; they overlap, so one move affects both tracks.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single piece. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click a highlighted target to jump. RULE: Jumps leap over adjacent pieces, removing the jumped piece upon landing. TRAP: Believing you must clear all pieces; the objective is strictly to leave exactly one survivor.

GOAL: Align yellow and orange markers to top and bottom slots. CONTROLS: Green arrows rotated rings clockwise; red arrows rotated them counter-clockwise. RULE: Left and right rings operated independently; rotating one did not affect the other. TRAP: Assuming red arrows rotated clockwise wasted time until you realized they were inverse controls.

GOAL: Merge two separate squares into a single cell by moving them through a narrow bridge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both squares simultaneously in the same direction. RULE: The squares merge when they occupy the same coordinate, ending the level immediately. TRAP: Assuming the squares swap positions when they collide; they actually overlap and combine into one entity.

GOAL: Match the bracketed panel’s pattern to its center glyph. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle colors; click glyphs to reveal the target mask. RULE: The white blocks in each panel’s center glyph define exactly which cells must be red. TRAP: Assuming the three outer panels interact with the target or that clicks on them affect the solution.

GOAL: Guide the three-point cluster to the target zone by shifting its center of mass. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move the head; click a member to swap its position with the head. RULE: The cluster’s center is the integer average of the three members’ coordinates, so spacing determines the pivot. TRAP: Assuming the head always leads; swapping members mid-path changes the shape and center, often blocking direct routes.

GOAL: Place yellow and orange markers at their target spots. CONTROLS: Green arrows rotate cycles forward; red arrows rotate backward. RULE: Row and column cycles share intersection points, allowing markers to switch tracks only at crossings. TRAP: Moving a marker along a single row or column without routing it through a shared intersection to transfer it to the other cycle.

GOAL: Light eight specific cells to match two overlapping glyph patterns that share a middle row. CONTROLS: Click a grid cell to toggle its color between blue and orange. RULE: Two separate three-by-three masks apply simultaneously; the shared row must satisfy both patterns at once. TRAP: Assuming the target color is red because the core looked red; it is actually orange.

GOAL: Slide the block into the ring's center hole. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; clicks select it. RULE: Dark frame pixels do not block movement, allowing entry. TRAP: Assuming the ring's border was solid and impassable.

GOAL: Rotate a hidden 21-tile loop to align matching symbols. CONTROLS: Top arrows shift the upper row segment; middle arrows turn the entire long path. RULE: The board is one continuous snake, not separate rows; the end wraps to the start. TRAP: Assuming the top and middle arrows control independent sections wastes moves tracking the hidden wrap-around.

GOAL: Guide the plug into the green socket by aligning its pins with the terminals. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the plug three cells in the chosen direction. RULE: The plug stops immediately when its edge touches the socket, ensuring a secure fit. TRAP: Moving down first causes a collision with the socket wall; always move left to clear the column before descending.

GOAL: Paint the grid to match four overlapping color masks. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color between red and orange. RULE: White pixels dictate the core’s color; gray pixels dictate the other. TRAP: Assuming red-core glyphs meant leaving cells red instead of following the white/gray pattern.

GOAL: Move a two-by-two block from the base to the far tip of the colored arm. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block two cells in the pressed direction; clicks confirmed moves. RULE: The block fits only if all four cells land on solid color, requiring precise alignment with the corridor. TRAP: Believing you could turn corners freely; the block’s square shape forces straight lines until a perfect fit appears.

GOAL: Slide the dark piece onto the yellow target to win. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the dark piece; the charcoal piece mirrors its position. RULE: Overlapping the yellow target triggers the win immediately, even if shapes aren't identical. TRAP: Assuming the static yellow piece moves or blocks the path wastes time; it is only a goal marker.

ESTABLISHED: The box moves; the red snake advances but reverts if the box leaves its path. Gray ghosts appear with lag but do not hold sockets or prevent reversion. FAILED: Holding the socket with a ghost; moving the box away and back to sustain the snake's advance; assuming ghosts stabilize the state. GOAL IS NOT: A simple box-to-ring transport, nor a mechanic relying on ghost persistence to lock the snake's position. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the box. The box pushes the snake head, which retracts upon the box's departure.

GOAL: Color every tile blue, red, or orange to match the hidden pattern. CONTROLS: Click a tile to cycle its color from blue to red to orange. RULE: White pixels in a glyph mean the tile matches the glyph's core color. TRAP: Assuming gray pixels mean blue; they actually mean the opposite of the core.

GOAL: Align the black piece so its mirror image covers the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; the bar reflects its position. RULE: The reflection is a perfect horizontal mirror across the central bar. TRAP: Moving the bar changes the reflection’s position, but moving the piece shifts both source and image together.

GOAL: Guide two squares to a shared center while a third dot acts as a static wall. CONTROLS: Arrows move all active pieces simultaneously; clicks select the dot to reposition it. RULE: Pieces cannot pass through walls or the dot, but bumping into the dot safely halts movement. TRAP: Assuming the dot must move with the squares wastes actions; park it early to create a barrier.

GOAL: Guide the box to the socket within the action budget. CONTROLS: Arrows move the box; Space resets the attempt. RULE: A ghost replays your previous moves, blocking the path if you overlap. TRAP: Assuming the ghost loops or bounces; it actually parks at the end of the recorded path.

GOAL: Align card classes to targets using minimal moves. CONTROLS: Arrows shift card positions; DOWN cycles classes forward. RULE: Class order forms a fixed cycle; shortest path is min(down, up). TRAP: Assuming UP always works; verify cycle direction before reversing.

ESTABLISHED: The side panel is a static image, not a mirror or progress bar. Pouring liquid only paints specific triangular regions; many cells remain unreachable. FAILED: Attempting to match the full square pattern to the panel by pouring liquid, as the physical constraints prevent filling the required cells. GOAL IS NOT: Filling the entire square to look like the panel, nor using the panel as a live display of your current state. CONTROLS: Rotation changes the pour direction. Pouring paints reachable cells. Clicking buttons triggers actions but did not clear the level.

ESTABLISHED: The token rises with water levels and is currently trapped in a sealed upper chamber capped by solid slabs. FAILED: Clicking blocks to alter water flow failed to open the ceiling or move the token upward. GOAL IS NOT: Simply raising the water level, as the token has nowhere to go. CONTROLS: Clicking removes blocks, draining water or releasing trapped sections, but does not directly move the token.

GOAL: Cross a vertical gap to reach the yellow core. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; clicking keys rotates structures. RULE: Rotating the red key creates a continuous bridge, regardless of turn direction. TRAP: Worrying about clockwise versus counter-clockwise rotation wastes time; both create the same path.

GOAL: Move two separate blocks to cover four target zones by positioning their bars correctly. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the selected block; Space cycles which block is active. RULE: Blocks only stop when they hit a wall or another block, not just any edge. TRAP: Assuming the first block could reach its final spot alone; you must move the second block to clear the path for the first.

GOAL: Assemble a cross by sliding three distinct shapes onto a hidden mirror image. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; Space cycles selection between pieces. RULE: Pieces only settle when their reflection perfectly aligns with the ghost outline. TRAP: Assuming pieces stack safely; they pass through each other, requiring precise final positioning to avoid misalignment.

GOAL: Move each shape to its matching color zone to cover all dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: A shape turns red only if its final resting position touches a red zone. TRAP: Assuming intermediate path touches count; only the final stop determines the color.

GOAL: Place yellow tiles in the two marked end slots. CONTROLS: Top buttons rotate the top row; middle buttons shift the entire serpentine path. RULE: The middle buttons move tiles along a single long loop connecting all squares. TRAP: Treating the top row as separate; it shares the leftmost square with the main loop.

GOAL: Route three yellow pieces to specific slots using ring rotations and arm shifts. CONTROLS: Click rings to cycle pieces along tracks; click arms to swap pieces between rings and connectors. RULE: Arms move pieces directly into connector positions, bypassing long ring paths for efficiency. TRAP: Assuming all pieces must travel the full ring distance; using arms saves critical clicks.

GOAL: Place yellow blocks into the two marked slots at the top corners. CONTROLS: Top arrows shift the top row left or right; side arrows rotate the main loop forward or backward. RULE: The side arrows move both yellow blocks along the loop simultaneously, so they must be positioned to land in the top row at the correct spots. TRAP: Assuming the top arrows move the yellow blocks directly; they only rearrange the top row, so you must use the loop arrows to bring the blocks up first.

GOAL: Place mirrors to reflect light onto every yellow tile. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected item; Space cycles selection between source, horizontal bar, and vertical bar.
